sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a house in Novi, Michigan?
sections.html:
A Novi homeowner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept an offer from a company that buys houses directly. All three paths finish at the same two places: the Novi assessing office for tax paperwork and the Oakland County Register of Deeds for the deed.

What differs is the calendar and what you carry into closing. A listing means showings, buyer financing and repair requests. A direct sale to an investor usually replaces those with a single negotiation, so compare the net figure on each offer rather than the headline price. The sections below cover the local steps that apply whichever route you pick.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Novi for a home seller?
sections.html:
Novi is an Oakland County city about 25 miles northwest of downtown Detroit. It covers 31.29 square miles, of which 30.25 are land, and Walled Lake is its largest lake. Three freeways meet here: I-96, I-696 and I-275, with M-5 close by, so a house near any of them is a short drive from most of metro Detroit (Wikipedia, Novi).

The place began as Novi Township in 1832 and became a city after voters approved a charter that took effect on February 24, 1969. Most of the housing you will see on a street map dates from the decades of fast suburban growth after that. Twelve Oaks Mall opened in 1977 and pulled shopping traffic, and later growth followed along the Novi Road and I-96 corridor.

Because the city sits on the Rouge River and Huron River watersheds, a few parcels on the north and west sides drain toward the Huron. Novi's forms page lists a Minor Land Improvement Permit that is required for any improvement that affects drainage on a property, so a regraded yard or new patio is worth checking against permit records.

sections.h2: How do Novi housing numbers compare with the rest of the area?
sections.html:
Novi is the most expensive of the four Michigan cities in this group of pages, with a median owner-occupied home value of $421,900 in the 2020 to 2024 survey period. The table below pulls the housing and population lines a seller is most likely to ask about.

sections.h2: Which schools and employers shape buyer demand in Novi?
sections.html:
Most of Novi sits in the Novi Community Schools district, which runs Novi High School, Novi Middle School and six elementary schools inside the city. The south side falls in Northville Public Schools, a pocket belongs to Walled Lake Consolidated Schools, and a small western strip is in South Lyon Community Schools. Check the district for your exact address, because it often decides which buyers show interest.

  • Retail: Twelve Oaks Mall plus car dealerships along Haggerty Road and Grand River Avenue.
  • Offices: ITC Transmission has its national headquarters here, and the Kroger Michigan regional office is on Grand River Avenue.
  • Health care: a 200-bed hospital campus opened in 2008 on a 200-acre parcel.
  • Auto suppliers: several Japanese and European automotive firms keep engineering and regional offices in Novi.

The Census Bureau counts 29.2% of Novi residents as foreign-born and 33.2% of people aged five and older as speaking a language other than English at home, which fits the international office base. Out-of-state and relocating buyers are a regular part of the market.

sections.h2: What does Novi's assessing office need when a house sells?
sections.html:
The city assessor handles four items you should expect to touch: the Property Transfer Affidavit, the principal residence exemption, appeals, and annual reappraisal. You can reach the Assessing Department at 248-347-0485.

  • Property Transfer Affidavit: Novi's forms page says state law requires it within 45 days of the transfer date.
  • Principal residence exemption: the exemption removes up to 18 mills of school operating tax, and the seller must file the rescission form with the assessor as soon as the home is sold. Late filing brings penalties and interest back to the date of the sale.
  • Conditional rescission: an owner who moved to a new Michigan principal residence may keep a conditional rescission on the old home for up to three years, but only while it is listed for sale, vacant, unrented and unused for business.
  • Board of Review: assessment protests need a petition filed with the board.

Novi appraisers visit parcels every year; the State Tax Commission recommends that assessors inspect 20% of properties annually, with photo updates and sometimes measurements. If you added a deck, finished space or a garage, expect the record card to be corrected. The poverty exemption application is heard at the July or December Board of Review each year and needs two years of tax returns and current account statements.

sections.h2: Do permits and occupancy paperwork affect a Novi sale?
sections.html:
Yes, because open or missing permits show up when a buyer's lender or inspector asks about them. Novi's forms page lists separate applications for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work, and a homeowner who acts as their own contractor must complete the Homeowner Permit Policy form.

The same page carries an occupancy request form for new construction and states that the Building Department needs two days' notice to process it. A temporary certificate of occupancy goes through the Administrative Board of Appeals. If you pulled permits for a kitchen, furnace, roof or addition, gather the final inspection records before you list or talk to a buyer. Ask the Novi Building Department for a copy of any record you cannot find.

sections.h2: What happens at the Oakland County Register of Deeds after a Novi closing?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded with the Oakland County Register of Deeds, which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. and can be reached at 248-858-0597. Recording a deed costs $30.00, a figure that already contains the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee.

A warranty deed must be tax certified by the Oakland County Treasurer first, and the county's fee page lists a $5.00 certificate. A title company normally handles both steps. The document needs a 2-1/2 inch top margin and a half inch on the other sides.

The county also posts its transfer tax rates: the county tax is $.55 per $500.00 and the state tax is $3.75 per $500.00 of consideration. Ask the title company to show these two lines on your settlement statement before you sign.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Novi without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, Novi has no local rule that forces repairs before a sale. Open permits and unpermitted work are the exception, so ask the Novi Building Department about permit history first. A buyer who pays cash may accept the house as it stands, while a financed buyer's lender can require fixes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file the Property Transfer Affidavit in Novi?
faqs.a: Novi's forms page says state law requires the affidavit within 45 days of the transfer. File it with the Novi assessor, and ask the title company whether it will submit it for you at closing.

faqs.q: What happens to my principal residence exemption when I sell in Novi?
faqs.a: You must rescind it. Novi's assessor says the rescission form is due as soon as the home is sold, rented or you move out, and late filing brings penalties and interest back to that date. A conditional rescission may apply for up to three years if the old house is vacant, listed and unrented.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Novi house?
faqs.a: The Oakland County Register of Deeds records it, not the city. The recording fee is $30.00 and a warranty deed needs a $5.00 treasurer's tax certificate, so most sellers let the title company submit the paperwork.

faqs.q: Which Novi school district will my buyer be in?
faqs.a: Most of Novi is in Novi Community Schools, but the south side is in Northville Public Schools, part is in Walled Lake Consolidated Schools and a small western section is in South Lyon Community Schools. Confirm the district with the school office for your address.
